pages.text: $(1)PROGRAM adder$(br)NOOP$(br)NOOP$(br)FUNCTION sum$(br)  PARAMETER n INTEGER$(br)  RESULT result INTEGER$(br)BEGIN$(br)  IF n = 0 ;$(br)  BEGIN$(br)    RETURN$(br)  END IF$(br)  CALL sum$()
$(1)    PARAMETER n n - 1 ;$(br)    RESULT result result$(br)  ASSIGN result result + n ;$(br)END FUNCTION$()
This function adds all numbers from 1 to $(1)n$(). It calls itself with $(1)n - 1$() until $(1)n$() is 0, then adds $(1)n$() on the way back. For $(1)n$() = 10, the result is 55.
To try it, put in an INTEGER variable item named $(1)n$(). Each call uses room on the cursor's stack, so very large numbers can crash it.
